newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tobacco stocks seen cheap on fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tobacco stocks seen cheap on fundamentals.

text.p: U.S. tobacco stocks advanced Monday on the view that recent quarterly results demonstrated the companies were very cheap in terms of fundamentals such as earnings growth rates and dividend yields.

"Philip Morris Cos Inc is selling at a 30 percent discount to the market," said analyst Emanuel Goldman af PaineWebber Group Inc. He said the risk that adverse court rulings will hurt the companies was already reflected in the share prices.
RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp was up 3/4 to 28-3/4 after Oppenheimer & Co raised its rating to buy from hold.

Oppenheimer analyst Roy Burry said that with RJR Nabisco trading at a 45 percent to 50 percent discount to the market, and supported by a dividend yield close to seven percent, "this is a record low valuation for the company."

Goldman said Philip Morris could be compared to Coca-Cola Co, which has about the same underlying growth rate in earnings per share as the tobacco-food company. He said with Coke's market premium and Philip Morris' discount, Morris was selling at about one-third the multiple of Coke.
"Philip Morris had incredibly strong earnings growth," said analyst Martin Feldman of Smith Barney Inc.

On October 22, Philip Morris reported third-quarter earnings rose to $2.01 per share from $1.71 a year ago, an 18 percent increase. Earnings per share in the first nine months of the year also showed an 18 percent gain.
Compared with consumer stocks in general, tobacco stocks could be playing "catch-up from last week, where not much happened," Feldman said.

He said RJR Nabisco surprised Wall Street last week with better-than-expected earnings. RJR Nabisco reported third-quarter earnings of $0.68 per share excluding a $0.02 charge. The company said it expected a strong fourth quarter.

Traders said RJR Nabisco was also getting a lift from renewed pressure from investor Carl Icahn to spin off its food unit. RJR Reynolds owns about 80 percent of Nabisco Holdings Corp, which trades on the New York Stock Exchange.
Burry said his target price on RJR Nabisco is #35 per share without a spinoff and $40-plus with a spinoff.
RJR Nabisco reiterated on Monday that it is committed to a spinoff but "at the right time."
The company wants to see some of the tobacco litigation resolved and investment grade ratings for both the food and tobacco entities, a spokeswoman said.

"(RJR Nabisco chief executive Steven) Goldstone is saying 'I will spin off the unit however I have to feel that the risk that I am taking is a prudent risk to be taking,'" Feldman said. In view of various lawsuits against the industry, Goldstone must be careful that any spinoff will withstand a potential legal challenge from lawyers representing smokers, Feldman said.

Feldman said if the industry wins cases brought by serveral state attorneys general over health care costs, or one or two of the cases brought by plaintiffs' attorney Norwod Wilner, that could be the catalyst for a spinoff.

On Tuesday, a court in Jacksonville, Fla. is scheduled to hear a formal motion on an effort to overturn a jury verdict in favor of one of Wilner's clients, Grady Carter. Last summer, a jury awarded ex-smoker Carter $750,000.
There has also been speculation that litigation against the industry could be settled, but Goldman said: "I don't think a settlement is within the realm of near-term possibility."
Philip Morris was up 1-1/4 to 93-3/4 in late trading and Brooke Group Ltd was up 1/2 to 5-1/4.
